findings.description: The backfill concurrency guarantee depends on a held ledger lock, but the plan does not pin the lock identity/protocol needed for atomic rename safety. Locking the ledger data file itself can still lose an append if a writer opens the old inode before the backfill rename and writes after replacement.
findings.recommendation: Pin a stable sidecar lock file or equivalent shared lock abstraction, require live append, compaction, and backfill to use it, and test the pre-open-before-rename append race explicitly.

findings.description: The plan consumes captured canonical-backfill evidence but does not define how the operator obtains that evidence while temp worktrees still exist, nor does it declare the evidence file as an explicit prepared prerequisite. Without that, the real historical dogfooding records can be impossible to backfill after temp cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Add a small evidence-capture feature or explicitly pin an operator-prepared prerequisite with required capture timing, sample artifact, and validation command before backfill implementation locks.

findings.description: F006 says zero or multiple observation mappings are rejected as malformed or ambiguous, while F002/F005 promise ambiguous records are skipped and reported in the per-record skipped list. The plan does not pin which evidence defects are file-fatal versus row-level skip reasons.
findings.recommendation: Split the C4 matrix into file-fatal schema errors and per-record unconfirmable mappings, then pin exit codes and report rows for each cell.

findings.description: The registered_stale JSON schema requires observed_count as an integer even when the registered repo has no observed row, but the plan never pins the emitted value. It also does not define whether the ledger adapter ignores invalid timestamps during aggregation or lets an invalid max last_seen fail the whole canonical row.
findings.recommendation: Pin absent-observation output as observed_count=0 and last_seen=null, and define timestamp aggregation as max valid timestamp with all-invalid rows failing closed, or explicitly choose the opposite.

findings.description: Reconcile rows are keyed by canonical_repo_key and the output has only one registry_name, but duplicate active registry entries can canonicalize to the same repo. The plan does not say whether to dedupe, choose a deterministic winner, emit a conflict, or return multiple rows with the same canonical key.
findings.recommendation: Pin duplicate registered-canonical handling before implementation, including deterministic registry_name selection or an explicit conflict classification.
